title: Kingdom Hearts Has Invaded Fortnite, And There’s A Lot To Collect
description: Kingdom Hearts has officially landed in Fortnite, and as expected, the update has brought plenty of cosmetics and weapons to the game. The content includes the Kingdom Key, a weapon Epic says can be used to clobber opponents and call down a shocking bolt of lightning when you need to clear the battlefield. If you're running low on health and shields, you can also grab a Sea Salt Ice Cream to top them up for the battles that lie ahead. But once you're underneath the heart-shaped moon on the ol' Fortnite island? That's when you can start using Kingdom Hearts Overrides to your advantage. Players can activate a Recovery Override to gain healing orbs whenever they eliminate another player equipped with a weapon, while the Level Up Override will spawn a Mythic Kingdom Key for each squad member at their current location. Players can also take part in the Kingdom Hearts Power Hour, starting on Saturday, September 19. This will take place at the following times: 11 AM PT - 1 PM / 2 - 4 PM ET 6 - 8 PM PT / 9 - 11 PM ET If you're looking to dress your Fortnite avatar up in some Kingdom Hearts threads, the new Sora, Riku, Kairi, and Roxas will be unlocked in the Fortnite Shop starting September 17 at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET. Each one comes with its own Back Bling, Pickaxe, and Lego Fortnite style. While Kingdom Hearts 4 will launch in 2027, it looks like Fortnite's crossover will help fill the gap until that long-awaited sequel finally arrives--plus, it's cathartic to see Kairi get a chance to kick some butt for once. Ahead of Kingdom Hearts 4's launch, it looks like the game was recently caught up in a massive data breach. If you're not afraid of spoilers, you can click through to take a look at the list of worlds that players can probably explore--if the leaked achievements are correct--which includes Coco and a few other surprise IP in the mix.

title: Xbox At Tokyo Game Show 2026: All The Biggest Announcements And Trailers
description: The Tokyo Game Show kicked off this week, and Xbox is celebrating its presence with a new broadcast dedicated to showing off what its Japanese partners are up to. The Japanese market has been a tough nut to crack for Microsoft--especially with Sony and Nintendo enjoying a home-field advantage--but Xbox has had a presence there for the last 20 years. Hosted by Misuzu Araki, this year’s Xbox TGS broadcast will offer exclusive content and new gameplay. It's also taking place at a very early hour, and we're betting that you might be sleeping through it. Fear not! As usual, we'll be covering all the announcements during the presentation, and you can scroll below to catch up on all the news and trailers. So, what can you expect from this year's livestream? Microsoft has confirmed that Minecraft Dungeons 2 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be on the show floor, so we wouldn't be too surprised to see new trailers for those games pop up. Gears of War: E-Day is also out soon, so that could be the focus of another trailer, and we're also expecting developers from across Japan and Asia to feature heavily in the broadcast. This was something that Sony did recently with its September State of Play livestream, as it dropped a bunch of trailers for upcoming games such as Stupid Never Dies, WPCA: World Phasebound Control Authority, and SlashZero. Gachiakuta: Breakout The show is kicking off with a new look at the Gachiakuta: Breakout game. If you haven't seen it, it's a pretty cool anime series about the value of trash--no really--and the manga source material is even better thanks to its cool illustrations. It looks like this will be a faithful adaptation, with plenty of action to enjoy. Crazy Taxi A new Crazy Taxi trailer? Yeah yeah yeah yeah! This fresh gameplay video shows off the new Japanese map you can explore with reckless abandon. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 The next Call of Duty game is out next month, and once again it looks like we're in for conspiracies,…

title: Hearthstone “Reign Of The Black Empire” Card Reveal – G’huun And Death Knight Control
description: Hearthstone's next expansion is Reign of the Black Empire, a journey back thousands of years into the distant past when the Old Gods were at war with the Titans. GameSpot has an exclusive reveal for a package of Death Knight class cards, including a big legendary that could swing the game in your favor--or even just win it outright. The three cards are blood runes, which emphasizes control and life-leeching effects. The first is Grafted Knight, a 2-blood rune, 2-mana 3/3 minion with Lifesteal. That's a solid early-game minion with good stats for the cost that should help you stay alive against aggressive decks in the early game. Hearthstone "Reign of the Black Empire" - Grafted Knight card Next up is Bloodfiend, a 3-blood rune, 4-mana 4/4 minion. It carries the battlecry "Spend up to 4 Corpses. Deal 1 damage to all other minions for each." That means it would hit your own minions, naturally, but as long as you've built up a pool of corpses, it's a good swingy card that can clear your opponent's mid-game board and still leave you with a body for them to deal with. Hearthstone "Reign of the Black Empire" - Bloodfiend card Finally we have the big one, G'huun, a legendary 3-blood rune, 8-mana minion with a mere 8/1 in stats. But don't let the statline fool you. G'huun has a battlecry that steals 6 from the lowest-health enemies by default, but then improves with every blood rune you play. So it will always drop as an 8/7, and will likely be much larger if you've built your deck around blood runes. The battlecry centering on the weakest enemies also means it could serve as a board clearer for smaller swarms. Hearthstone "Reign of the Black Empire" - G'huun card But for particularly ambitious Death Knights, G'huun could serve as a finisher, or even a one-turn kill. The battlecry steals health from the lowest-health enemies, not just minions, which means the enemy hero is fair game. That could finish off your opponent if their health is low enough, or just target them…

title: Metroid Ravenous Logo Memes Make Phrases Like “Girl Dinner” And “They Took My Ass” Look So Metal
description: Hype emanating from the reveal of Metroid Ravenous has translated into an onslaught of memes after a logo generator circulated online. If you're on Reddit or Bluesky, you may have seen the instantly iconic image of Samus Aran aggressively pinning down a mysterious enemy for consumption, but now accompanied by stupid text like "I ASKED FOR NO PICKLES" in the Metroid Ravenous font. The Pixelframe Design website unveiled a tool that lets anyone input any text and style it to look like the grainy and jagged Metroid Ravenous logo, with four options for the image background. Pixelframe Design previously made similar logo generators for games like GTA 6, The Duskbloods, and famously, Pokopia. The apparent hook of Metroid Ravenous is Samus's need to kill and consume her enemies to survive. Naturally, that has led to food-related memes like a riff on the "55 burgers" scene from I Think You Should Leave, a reference to the viral concept of "girl dinner," or a simple but effective "Om Nom Nom" joke. Literally any wording you put into the generator will look more badass in this font. It's also been amusing to see other video game titles like Hello Kitty Island Adventure in the Ravenous font face, and several other of these memes are just vulgar and gross enough to be hilarious. Don't expect any of this to become official Nintendo marketing material. The Metroid subreddit was briefly jam-packed with these images, leading to moderators creating a megathread devoted to the meme template. Hilariously, many of the top-upvoted comments are Ravenous memes dunking on the mods. Revealed during the September 2026 Nintendo Direct, Metroid Ravenous is a follow-up to 2021's Metroid Dread and a return to the 2D track of the franchise. While Nintendo hasn't officially commented on who is developing Ravenous, Dread studio MercurySteam hinted that it's behind the upcoming title on social media. Metroid Ravenous releases on January 28, 2027, and a special edition coming with a steelbook and…

title: Resident Evil Director Was In Horrible Pain Making The Movie
description: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has revealed he was going through hell while making the movie, which is about a man going through hell. He told The Hollywood Reporter that he had pneumonia for the first half of filming on Resident Evil. For the second half of production, he had Campylobacter jejuni. This causes diarrhea, and man, that sucks for anyone, but especially if you're trying to film a big-budget, highly anticipated film based on a property with legions of fans and great expectations creatively and commercially. "So I was very, very ill for the whole production, and everything felt so barely in control because my body was failing me," Cregger explained. Cregger said he credits his "wonderful, talented" department leads to help him through, while he also praised Resident Evil star Austin Abrams for going above and beyond. He said Abrams is "one of the most can-do, positive people I’ve ever met. I was spoiled by the people around me." Not only was Cregger physically sick while making Resident Evil, he had to deal with freezing-cold conditions in the north of the Czech Republic where the movie was filmed. "We froze our asses off," he said. This wasn't the first time Cregger was dealing with physical turmoil while making a movie. On his last film, Weapons, it was so hot and humid that he needed an IV and directed scenes remotely. Resident Evil releases on September 18, and it's expected to have a huge, record-setting opening weekend. The movie stars Austin Abrams as a medical courier named Bryan who is an "idiot" everyman who finds himself in a world of pain.

title: Nintendo’s Customer Appreciation Sale Flubbed The Goodwill Gesture Attempt
description: I love Nintendo. It was a formative part of my video game history, and to this day I think it makes some of the most consistently great games in the industry. But you know what I love more? Deals. For proof just look at my Steam backlog, which is full of games I stupidly bought on the basis of their being cheap. Do I have time to play this? No, but it was so cheap! This is somewhat of a contradiction in my gaming tastes. Nintendo isn't known for offering sales. In fact, it's notoriously stingy with discounts, offering them rarely, and with only modest savings. So I was cautiously optimistic about the Customer Appreciation Sale, which Nintendo promoted as a larger scale sale than usual. The sale is now ongoing and, well, I should have trusted my instincts. These deals are not good. The sale prices are relegated primarily to older games, and while 30% is a larger discount than usual for Nintendo games on the eShop, it still barely makes a dent in the full list price. Since Nintendo games keep their sticker price for years, this sale boasts discounts on years-old games like Donkey Kong Tropical Freeze and Mario Tennis Aces, both from 2018, for a lean $42. Those hoping that newer games would be included are likely left disappointed. A handful of 2025 releases are included--Metroid Prime 4, the Mario Galaxy two-pack, Xenoblade Chronicles Definitive Edition, and Donkey Kong Returns HD. Everything else is 2024 and before. So it's mostly older games, and most of the newest games are ports of older games. And in many cases these are the Switch 1 versions of games, meaning that if you want an optional Switch 2 upgrade, you have to make two purchases, and end up with less than a 30% discount as a result. What a savings So the deals are unremarkable. But so what? I've gone this long without a copy of Astral Chain; I don't need to buy it now for $42. What makes this sale such an unforced error, though, is how Nintendo positioned the sale as innately tied to tariffs. When…

title: Resident Evil Is Now The Highest-Rated Gaming Movie Ever
description: The Resident Evil movie from Weapons and Barbarian director Zach Cregger releases in theaters on September 18. Reviews from critics went live today, and the movie is earning high scores. GameSpot's Resident Evil review scored it an 8 and said it successfully captures the breathless terror of the games. In fact, it's now the highest-rated video game movie ever. It boasts a mightily impressive 96% on Rotten Tomatoes from 71 reviews and an equally impressive 80 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic. According to Metacritic, Resident Evil is the highest-rated video game movie ever, well ahead of another 2026 movie, Exit 8, which has a 71 Metascore. The six Resident Evil movies that Paul W.S. Anderson made did not score very high with critics, with 2016's The Final Chapter topping them all at 49% on Metacritic. The latest Resident Evil movie before Cregger's, 2021's Welcome to Raccoon City from director Johannes Roberts, scored a 44% on Metacritic. After that movie came out, Constantin, which has owned the movie rights to Resident Evil since the '90s, intended to put the franchise on hiatus. However, Cregger, coming off the success of Barbarian, pitched Constantin on his new, original take, and Constantin loved it so much that they put it into production. Video game movies had a track record of mediocrity at best for years, but the tide is turning in recent times. This could be for many different reasons, but some have theorized that part of what made video game movies of yesteryear poor in terms of reception was that, in large part, the game studios and creative minds behind them were not involved in the development process. That's changed now. Oliver Berben, the CEO of Constantin, said that while his team didn't contractually need to consult with Capcom, the film studio did so anyway to ensure it was respecting and caring for the IP and its fans. That might be a surprise to some gamers, as many have voiced their concerns and dislike for Cregger's take on Resident Evil,…

title: WoW: Forever Is More Than Classic+, It’s WoW 2
description: Going into BlizzCon 2026, World of Warcraft Classic fans, myself included, were hoping for what the community coined as Classic+. Instead, what we got is essentially WoW 2, an alternate vision for what Blizzard's legendary MMORPG called World Of Warcraft: Forever. It wasn't long after Blizzard re-released WoW Classic, the original version of its genre-defining MMO, in 2019 that players started to dream about what might come next. A community that was at one time dominated by calls for Blizzard to make "no changes" to WoW Classic and keep the game as it was two decades ago gave way to an entirely different desire: more. Sure, it was fantastic and nostalgic to return to the original version of Azeroth and old-school WoW's slower and more methodical gameplay, but what if there were substantial changes and additions? What if there were major class balance changes to make more playstyles viable? What if Blizzard finished zones that were infamously half-baked in the original game? What if some of the zones long teased on the original WoW's map, like Mount Hyjal, were actually accessible? What if there were new dungeons and endgame content instead of the same Molten Core and Onyxia raids players have completed dozens upon dozens of times over the years? The list of possibilities felt endless, but the exact requests and no-nos differed depending on who you asked. As WoW: Forever senior game designer Josh Greenfield told me in an interview at BlizzCon, the "old adage" for Classic+ has always been "ask 10 different people what they want [and] you'll get 11 different answers." Somehow, WoW: Forever is going above and beyond those community expectations, in often-surprising ways. After going hands-on with WoW: Forever for around two hours at BlizzCon ahead of the game's closed beta on September 17, I can safely say it delivers on many of the changes the community has wanted over the years. But it's also so much more--a fascinating blend of old and new that on the surface may…

title: GTA 5's 'Become a celebrity' mod is almost weirdly fully featured
Lego Batman: Legacy Of The Dark Knight Gives Harley Quinn An Arkham Asylum Makeover
description: Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight was a fun tribute to the Caped Crusader when it launched earlier this year, but if you're tired of saving Gotham, you can embrace chaos with two of the city's greatest villains: Harley Quinn and the Joker. The duo are headlining the game's Mayhem Collection expansion, and just like Batman, they're dressing in style with multiple outfits that you can unlock during their caper. GameSpot can exclusively reveal one of them: a classic costume for Harley Quinn, pulled directly from 2009's Batman: Arkham Asylum. And still one of Harley's best outfits. While Harley Quinn predominantly wore a jester's outfit throughout her appearances in Batman: The Animated Series and related comic books, Rocksteady's Arkham Asylum game saw her switch up her look dramatically for what can best be described as a doctor-themed dominatrix. Out with the spandex onesie, in with a repurposed doctor's outfit, leather corset, domino mask, and other elements that paid homage to her roots. In Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, this costume is described as having prankster pigtails and a "chaotic" corset. In case you missed it, the Mayhem Collection draws heavily from Batman: The Animated Series, with developer TT Games calling the expansion a love letter to the landmark '90s show that introduced Harley Quinn as the Joker's sidekick. Fans can find several references to the series in the Mayhem Collection, along with Easter eggs for other Batman shows, films, games, and comic book stories. There's even a nod to Harley Quinn's original voice actor, the late Arleen Sorkin, and the new story mission chronicles the first meeting between the Joker and Quinn, back when she was still the ambitious psychiatrist Dr. Harleen Quinzel. The Mayhem Collection launches on September 18 for Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, one of the best games of 2026. It's also coming to Switch 2 on the same day, and it's also available for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave’s Fantastic Reviews Have Me Feeling FOMO
description: Here we go again: A new Fire Emblem game is garnering glowing reviews, and I'm thinking this could be the one that finally clicks with me. Launching tomorrow on Switch 2, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave sits at a fantastic 89 metascore (at the time of publication) on GameSpot's sister site Metacritic. That's good enough to place it No. 13 currently on Metacritic's list for best games of 2026. In addition, GameSpot's Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave review says this is "the new high point to beat for future entries." As someone who didn't plan to buy the strategy RPG, I'm now second-guessing myself. I have a history of buying well-reviewed Fire Emblem games, trying them out for maybe five hours, and then bouncing off them for something else. That was especially true of Fire Emblem: Three Houses on Switch in 2019. Before that, my first foray into the series came in 2013 with Fire Emblem Awakening on the Nintendo 3DS, if you don’t consider me maining Marth in Super Smash Bros. Melee. This is a game I still have downloaded on my 3DS XL, which sits in the drawer of my bedside table. I've tried so many times to engage with the game, only to stop after a couple of hours. Once again, I don't dislike the turn-based action, but for some reason, it never fully connects. I'm obviously in the minority, because Fire Emblem Awakening basically saved the entire series. Those previous encounters with the Fire Emblem franchise had me ignoring Fortune's Weave, until now. I see the high praise for the Switch 2 exclusive and feel like I might be missing out on an amazing game. Sure, I'm currently in the middle of playing Blasphemous and have Final Fantasy 7 Remake waiting for me after picking it up on sale. But what if Fortune's Weave is the Fire Emblem game that finally, finally resonates with me? Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave launches tomorrow, September 17, on Switch 2. 28 Best Nintendo Switch 2 Games To Play Right Now View Images

title: Call Of Duty: Black Ops Dev Teases “Something That Nobody’s Ever Experienced Before”
description: Veteran Call of Duty developer Treyarch is finishing up its work on Black Ops 7 and shifting to its next project, but what will that be? That remains to be seen, but Treyarch design director Kevin Drew said in a new Dev Talk video that it might not be what you expect. Drew said Treyarch has "learned a lot" working on 2024's Black Ops 6 and 2025's Black Ops 7 and "tried a lot of things in our current era." "But we're ready to make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before," he said. That sounds hyperbolic and extreme, and Call of Duty studios are definitely known for grandiose claims. Treyarch created the Black Ops series, which debuted in 2010, and it remains one of the most popular brands within the franchise. In an unusual move, back-to-back Black Ops games came out in 2024 and 2025, and Treyarch itself admitted it did worry about franchise fatigue. EA's Battlefield 6 outsold Black Ops 7 in 2025, with Black Ops 7 falling down to the No. 5 spot for the year, at least in the US. In another big shakeup for Call of Duty, and seemingly in a bid to sell more units, Microsoft announced that Call of Duty games will no longer be included with Xbox Game Pass at launch, beginning with this year's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Infinity Ward is leading development on Modern Warfare 4, though, as usual, Activision's network of Call of Duty studios, including Treyarch, are expected to contribute to the game's overall development. An interesting rumor making the rounds related to Call of Duty claims that Microsoft--which owns Call of Duty and Activision--is considering having a Call of Duty studio work on a Halo game. Another rumor said Microsoft could "put Halo under Activision" as part of a larger restructuring to help Halo regain its prominence in the FPS market.

title: Resident Evil Finally Captures The Breathless Terror Of The Games
description: Few movies can truly say they hit the ground running, but Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is among them. And that’s a good thing, because after so many Resident Evil movies, every new one needs a running start to have a chance of making it. We can’t talk about a Resident Evil movie without doing a little bit of table-setting first, though. Resident Evil debuted on PlayStation in 1996 and coined the name for an emerging game genre: Survival Horror. Since then, Paul W.S. Anderson has directed six live-action Resident Evil movies starring his photogenic and acrobatic wife Milla Jovovich. 2021 brought us the Robbie Amell-led Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City. That’s not counting the half-dozen CGI Resident Evil movies that more or less act as canonical extensions of the game series. Generally speaking, the Resident Evil movies have been on a downward trend since early into Anderson’s tenure. Now, in 2026, the unkillable movie franchise rises again, this time with Zach Cregger, director of Barbarian and Weapons, acting as the head of the monster. Resident Evil follows medical courier Bryan (Austin Abrams) as he drops off a package and argues with his girlfriend over the phone. Instead of going home to talk to her about it, though, Bryan jumps at the chance to take a high-priority delivery to Raccoon City. It needs to get there intact, and without any detours. A perfect way to not talk about any personal problems Bryan might have. Bryan starts questioning his decision when he hits a woman in a nightgown while driving in the dark down a slick road in heavy snow. That moment marks the point in which Bryan is in over his head and finds himself in a race to survive. Bryan is not a hero. He is perhaps the least heroic character to lead a Resident Evil movie. And that’s a huge factor in why this disgusting, hilarious, and often frightening movie works. Bryan doesn’t have special forces training, and like so many of us, he’s only ever wielded a gun using a video game…
